microtheory.name: adaptive_tiered_dispatch
microtheory.definition: L2 dynamic composition pattern. Names the recipe Jabberwock's vocabulary surfaced for runtime-adaptive dispatch: per-kind hot counters drive a tier-up policy that compiles hot rules into JIT artefacts cached per (kind, Γ_epoch); inline caches accelerate per-call-site dispatch; Γ mutations (Axiom 3) bump the epoch, invalidating downstream artefacts; deoptimisation falls back to interpreter when a guard fails; the scheduler's own state is graph data so it can observe and adjust itself (second-order cybernetics). Each piece exists in other Mts (compilers' tiered_compilation + OSR + inline_cache; realtime_systems' EDF + deadline_inheritance + anytime_algorithms; reflection_metaprogramming's operations_on_grammar + intercession; optimal_estimation_control's adaptive_control + gain_scheduling; cybernetics_systems' variety_requisite + second_order_cybernetics); this Mt names how they fit together for L2.

concepts.name: adaptive_tiered_dispatch_pattern
concepts.definition: The composition pattern. Submits flow through a base EDF scheduler (l2_dispatch::Scheduler); each Task carries a kind (Sym); a HotCounter records per-kind fires; when a kind crosses TierUpPolicy.threshold, the dispatcher emits a TierUp signal; an asynchronous compile pass produces a CompiledArtefact stamped with the current Γ epoch; subsequent submits for that kind use the artefact through an InlineCache; Γ mutations bump the epoch, marking artefacts stale; stale lookups deopt back to interpreter; the scheduler's own state lives in the graph (Axiom 3) so reflexes can observe + reconfigure it.

concepts.name: hot_counter_per_kind
concepts.definition: Component 1. Per-rule-kind atomic counter incremented on every submit. Atomic so worker threads don't contend on the counter itself; lookup map uses a sharded lock for the first-fire creation. Snapshot iteration gives a profile (kind, count) the rest of the system uses for cooling decisions. Substrate analogue: substrate's HotCounter struct.

concepts.name: tier_up_policy_threshold
concepts.definition: Component 2. Configurable count above which a kind is considered hot enough to compile. Default 100 — matches the substrate's typical 'one rare rule fires a few times, one hot rule fires thousands' distribution. Higher threshold: less compile work, slower hot path; lower: more compile, faster hot path. Per-class thresholds possible (HardRealtime lower than BestEffort).

concepts.name: gamma_epoch_counter
concepts.definition: Component 3. Monotonically-increasing AtomicU64 bumped by the substrate on every Γ mutation. Sole source of truth for 'has the rule store changed since I compiled?'. Bumped using Release ordering; read with Acquire so workers observe the bump after any graph mutation that preceded it.

concepts.name: compiled_artefact_cache
concepts.definition: Component 4. Map Sym→CompiledArtefact<T> where T is the compiled payload (substrate_rs uses jit::JittedFn). Each artefact carries epoch_at_compile. Lookups check current epoch against stamp; mismatch ⇒ artefact stale, treated as cache miss + deoptimisation. evict_stale() bulk-drops stale entries on demand.

concepts.name: inline_cache_per_callsite
concepts.definition: Component 5. Per-dispatch-site cache mapping observed kind → resolved compiled artefact pointer. Avoids the per-call HashMap lookup once the site stabilises. Polymorphic inline cache (PIC) for sites that see multiple kinds. Invalidated alongside the underlying artefact when epoch bumps.

concepts.name: tracing_vs_method_jit_choice
concepts.definition: Component 6. Method JIT compiles whole rules; tracing JIT compiles hot paths through them (loop bodies, common branches). Tracing wins on rules with predictable inner loops (audio frame processing); method wins on rules whose branching is data-dependent. Substrate uses method JIT for the v1 (jit.rs is whole-Term-tree); tracing is a future extension.

concepts.name: speculation_with_guards
concepts.definition: Component 7. JIT'd code makes assumptions about kind layout, attr presence, neighbour cardinality. Each assumption is encoded as a guard that branches to deopt on failure. Guard failure rate is tracked; rules with high guard-fail rates get less-speculative recompiles.

concepts.name: deoptimisation_on_stack_replacement
concepts.definition: Component 8. When a guard fails (or epoch mismatch detected mid-run), the JIT'd frame is unwound + the interpreter resumes from the equivalent Term-tree position. OSR (on-stack replacement) handles the transition. The interpreted run is always correct; the JIT is an acceleration.

concepts.name: deadline_inheritance_for_shared_rule_state
concepts.definition: Component 9. When a hot rule fires while another rule holds shared graph state, the holder inherits the waiter's deadline (RT priority inheritance generalised to deadline semantics). Bounds priority inversion in the dispatcher. Realtime_systems' deadline_inheritance applied at the rule-firing layer.

concepts.name: anytime_degradation_under_overload
concepts.definition: Component 10. When dispatcher utilisation > 1.0 (more work than deadline can fit), BestEffort tasks degrade to coarser results or skip; SoftRealtime keeps target deadlines; HardRealtime always completes. Realtime_systems' anytime_algorithms applied at the dispatch layer.

concepts.name: second_order_scheduler_state_as_graph
concepts.definition: Component 11. The scheduler's runtime state (current epoch, hot counters, cached artefacts metadata, current load) is graph data the substrate's reflexes can observe and rules can mutate. A reflex can adjust the tier-up threshold based on observed hot-counter distribution (gain scheduling); a rule can bump the epoch manually for testing. Axiom 3 + cybernetics' second_order_cybernetics applied to the dispatcher itself.

concepts.name: axiom3_satisfied_via_gamma_epoch
concepts.definition: Invariant: every artefact carries epoch_at_compile; lookups check current epoch; mismatch deopts. Paper 1 Axiom 3 ('Π includes operations that observe, predicate over, and extend G from within G') is honoured because Γ mutations are observed (by the epoch counter) and propagate (via cache invalidation) without out-of-band machinery.

concepts.name: correctness_via_interpreter_fallback
concepts.definition: Invariant: deoptimisation always lands on the interpreter, which is correct by construction (it walks the canonical Term-tree). The JIT can have bugs, be conservative, get out of date — the interpreter is the safety net. No path executes JIT'd code in violation of the current Γ.

concepts.name: schedulability_under_dynamic_load
concepts.definition: Invariant: utilisation U = Σ(C_i / T_i) must stay ≤ 1.0 for HardRealtime. Adaptive policy (gain scheduling) adjusts BestEffort throughput downward when HardRealtime utilisation rises. Ashby's law of requisite variety: regulator's adaptation rate must match load-change rate.

concepts.name: bounded_deopt_amortised_cost
concepts.definition: Invariant: deoptimisation cost (frame unwind + interpreter resume) is bounded. Profile-driven recompiles use the guard-failure record to be less speculative on the retry, so a hot rule can't enter a deopt-recompile-deopt loop. K consecutive deopts cool the kind back to interpreted-only.

concepts.name: reflective_transparency_of_dispatcher
concepts.definition: Invariant: every dispatcher state (hot counts, cached artefacts, current policy parameters) is reflectively accessible as graph data. A rule asking 'what's hot?' walks the same graph as a rule asking 'what's blue?'. No special-case APIs for introspecting the dispatcher.

concepts.name: tradeoff_tier_up_threshold
concepts.definition: Tradeoff: low threshold → compiles more rules, faster hot path, more compile-time overhead + memory; high threshold → fewer compiles, slower hot path. Per-class tuning common (HardRealtime threshold lower because deadline cost of interpretation is asymmetric). substrate_rs default: 100.

concepts.name: tradeoff_speculation_vs_deopt_cost
concepts.definition: Tradeoff: aggressive speculation (assume monomorphic, assume attr present) → faster JIT'd code BUT more deopts on Γ change or polymorphic call. Conservative speculation → slower JIT'd code, fewer deopts. Profile-guided choice per kind.

concepts.name: tradeoff_epoch_granularity
concepts.definition: Tradeoff: bump epoch per Γ mutation (fine-grained, accurate, but cache thrashes on bulk updates) vs per batch (coarse, but cache may serve stale during the batch's window). substrate_rs choice: per-mutation by default, batched explicitly via a 'mutation_batch' guard the caller opts into.

concepts.name: tradeoff_hot_counter_locality
concepts.definition: Tradeoff: single global HashMap<Sym, Atomic> (low memory, lock-on-first-create contention) vs per-thread shards merged on snapshot (no contention, larger memory). substrate_rs uses single map with sharded creation lock; works because hot kinds are few + creation is one-shot.

concepts.name: tradeoff_eviction_policy
concepts.definition: Tradeoff: never evict (lowest re-compile cost, unbounded memory) vs LRU (bounded memory, occasional re-compile) vs cool-on-deopt (rules that deopt frequently freed first). substrate_rs starts with never-evict + explicit evict_stale() on epoch bump; LRU is a future enhancement.

concepts.name: substrate_rs_canonical_instance
concepts.definition: substrate_rs is the canonical instance. l2_dispatch::Scheduler (committed 3c791f8) provides the EDF base. Planned: l2_adaptive::AdaptiveDispatcher wrapping Scheduler with HotCounter + Epoch + CompiledCache<T> + TierUpPolicy + DispatchOutcome enum. jit.rs (existing) supplies T = JittedFn for the cached payload. Integration with substrate's run_rules loop is the followup commit.

concepts.name: hotspot_tiered_jit_reference
concepts.definition: Java HotSpot's tiered compilation. C1 (fast compile, less optimised) then C2 (slower compile, fully optimised). Profile-driven; OSR for tier-up inside hot loops. Reference architecture for tier_up_policy_threshold + tracing_vs_method_jit_choice + speculation_with_guards components.

concepts.name: v8_inline_cache_reference
concepts.definition: Google V8's PIC (polymorphic inline cache). Per-call-site cache that adapts from monomorphic to polymorphic to megamorphic. Reference for inline_cache_per_callsite. Demonstrates speculation_with_guards via hidden-class checking.

concepts.name: luajit_trace_compilation_reference
concepts.definition: LuaJIT's trace JIT. Compiles hot loops as linear traces, with side exits for guard failures. Aggressive speculation + cheap deopt. Reference for tracing_vs_method_jit_choice (the tracing-JIT alternative) + deoptimisation_on_stack_replacement.

concepts.name: pypy_meta_tracing_reference
concepts.definition: PyPy's meta-tracing. Trace through the interpreter itself; specialise to the executed program. Most reflective option, closest to the substrate's Axiom-3 framing (the interpreter IS Π, traceable as Γ subgraph).

concepts.name: naming_the_composition_makes_l5_integration_obvious
concepts.definition: Meta. Before this Mt, jit.rs existed as a primitive but its connection to scheduling was implicit. Now the pattern names HOW the JIT plugs in: as the compile target whose output populates CompiledCache<JittedFn>, triggered by HotCounter crossing TierUpPolicy.threshold, invalidated by Epoch bumps the substrate emits on Γ mutation. The L5 integration becomes a wiring task, not a design task.

concepts.name: second_order_observability_compounds
concepts.definition: Meta. Because the scheduler's state is graph data (Axiom 3 honoured at the dispatcher level), Jabberwock's reflexes can observe + adjust dispatch policy at runtime: tier-up threshold tuned by observed hot-counter distribution; epoch-bump frequency tuned by observed deopt rate; eviction tuned by observed memory pressure. The dispatcher becomes part of the substrate it dispatches for.

rules.name: gamma_change_must_bump_epoch
rules.head: Jabberwock mutates the Γ rule store
rules.body: the substrate MUST bump the gamma_epoch_counter after the mutation, with Release ordering so subsequent epoch reads observe the change. Any cached compiled artefact stamped with the prior epoch becomes stale on the next lookup.

rules.name: tier_up_fires_exactly_at_threshold
rules.head: Jabberwock's HotCounter records the Nth fire for kind K where N == TierUpPolicy.threshold
rules.body: submit returns DispatchOutcome::TierUp { kind: K, count: N }. The next submit returns Queued. The caller acts on TierUp by triggering an asynchronous compile pass; subsequent submits use the cached artefact once it's installed.

rules.name: deopt_lands_on_interpreter_always
rules.head: Jabberwock's JIT'd code hits a guard failure or sees an epoch mismatch
rules.body: execution must unwind to the interpreter resuming at the equivalent Term-tree position. The interpreter is correct-by-construction; the JIT is an acceleration. No path executes JIT'd code against a Γ it wasn't compiled against.

rules.name: policy_parameters_live_in_graph
rules.head: Jabberwock asks 'what's the current tier-up threshold?'
rules.body: answer comes from walking dispatcher state in the graph, not from a private dispatcher field. A reflex can adjust the threshold by writing graph data; the dispatcher reads its parameters from the graph on the next tick.

rules.name: schedulability_under_adaptation_requires_variety_match
rules.head: Jabberwock's dispatcher adapts policy under changing load
rules.body: Ashby: adaptation rate must equal or exceed load-change rate to maintain U ≤ 1 for HardRealtime. If load changes faster than the gain scheduler can track, HardRealtime deadlines slip. Monitor adaptation lag explicitly.

rules.name: guard_failure_cools_speculation
rules.head: Jabberwock's JIT'd kind hits its Nth consecutive guard failure
rules.body: N consecutive failures (e.g. 3) cool the kind back to interpreted-only for M ticks. Avoids the deopt-recompile-deopt loop. Re-tier-up only after sustained interpreted hotness.
